antivirus.title: Lightweight Mode Anti-Kill Guide
antivirus.whyTitle: Why does Lightweight Mode get terminated?
antivirus.why: Lightweight Mode destroys the WebView2 UI process to save memory while keeping only the tray icon and proxy core in the background. Some optimizers (such as 360 Safe) track apps that previously opened and then closed a window, and forcefully kill them as leftover processes under high CPU load (360's standard Trust Zone does not prevent this).
antivirus.easyTitle: Option 1: Effortless Stealth Mode (Recommended for Daily Use)
antivirus.easyBody: With "Silent Start" enabled, Clash Mini goes straight into the system tray without creating or showing the main window—on boot, shortcut launch, or relaunch after termination. If the main window is never exposed, 360 will not flag or kill it.
antivirus.easyWarning: ⚠️ Note: With this option, avoid left-clicking the tray icon to open the main window during daily use. Once the window has been shown and closed, closing back to tray can still trigger cleanup under high CPU load (if terminated, click the launch shortcut again to silently restore tray residency).
